zh-CN.title: 反馈
zh-CN.context: 别人指出问题、要求修改或评价你的表达和成果时。
zh-CN.typical_response: 这类场景容易把事实信息和关系信号混在一起：你可能先感到被评价、被误解，或急着证明自己。

en.title: Feedback
en.context: When someone points out a problem, asks for changes, or evaluates your work or communication.
en.typical_response: This scene can blend factual input with relationship signals: you may first feel evaluated, misunderstood, or pushed to explain yourself.
en.strength: It can help you separate the information being offered from the emotion it triggers.
en.cost: If feedback is read as a judgment of you as a person, it can lead to defensiveness, over-explaining, or missing useful information.
en.better_move: Ask for one concrete point first, then decide whether to explain, adjust, or observe further.
en.one_sentence_script: Which part would you most like me to adjust: the outcome, the process, or the way I communicated?

zh-CN.title: 冲突
zh-CN.context: 意见分歧、语气升高、彼此防御或问题迟迟无法推进时。
zh-CN.typical_response: 冲突会放大你对情绪、关系和控制感的处理方式：你可能先解释、先压住、先照顾别人，或先退开。

en.title: Conflict
en.context: When disagreement, sharper tone, mutual defensiveness, or stalled problem-solving appears.
en.typical_response: Conflict amplifies how you handle emotion, relationship tension, and control: you may explain, contain, take care of others, or step back first.
en.strength: This cue can show what you tend to protect first under pressure.
en.cost: If treated as a fixed reaction style, it may ignore power differences, safety risks, and the other person’s behavior.
en.better_move: Narrow the conflict to one workable issue; if there is threat, humiliation, or coercive pressure, prioritize safety and support.

zh-CN.title: 关系边界

en.title: Relationship boundary
en.context: When someone expects understanding, help, concession, emotional availability, or a change in your pace.
en.typical_response: Boundary moments are usually not about caring less; they are about separating understanding from what you can realistically carry.
en.strength: It helps you separate care, responsibility, and available capacity.
en.cost: If empathy is the only focus, another person’s emotional load can become your long-term obligation.
en.better_move: Acknowledge the feeling, then name what you can and cannot take on right now.

en.title: Pressure recovery

en.typical_response: Recovery scenes look at how you return to a workable state after emotional load, not whether you are “calm enough.”
